title: CANcestry hardware simulation case (v0.1.0)
description: Schema for a hardware simulation case (issue #33, H-01; HwAGENTS.md rule 3 and rule 5, virtual-bench-plan §6). A sim case declares, before the model is simulated: the requirement under test, the Modelica model, the parameter set (which hw/tests/test_power_sim.py cross-checks against the schema-validated BOM extract under hw/bom/), the acceptance tolerance, the oracle that must witness the result (rule 3: no oracle ID, no pass) and the fixed seeds. Determinism is mandatory (HwAGENTS.md rule 5): a sim case with no stochastic content declares an empty seed list; seeds must be integers when present.

case_id.description: Stable case identifier; the evidence artifact is hw/tests/evidence/<case_id>.json.

scenario.description: Human-readable statement of the scenario, including which sub-events of the requirement it covers and which it does not.

not_covered.description: Sub-events or aspects of the requirement this case does NOT cover (honest ledger, HwAGENTS.md rule 4).

model.description: Qualified Modelica class name inside hw/model/CancestryLib/.

parameters.description: Model parameters for this case; every value must match the cited BOM extract (checked by hw/tests/test_power_sim.py).

tolerances.description: Acceptance tolerances declared by the case (e.g. vb_max_abs_delta_v).

seeds.description: Fixed random seeds. Empty when the case has no stochastic content (determinism, HwAGENTS.md rule 5).

solver.description: Uniform trace sampling by default. pulse_features uses fixed interval counts around each oracle pulse feature, with step_s as the maximum communication step and stop_s as the per-pulse time ceiling (HW-FR-004).
